items.title: 52157_Count Basie oral history interview
items.q: "In addition to Walter Page and Jimmy Rushing, there are Ed Lewis, my first trumpet player of long standing, Jack Washington, baritone sax and Jo Jones at the drums."

ctx.x: So he of his own accord went into the Army. I mean, not of his own accord --
No, no. Jo Jones He and JoJo both.

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: working with Bill Basie and Freddie Green in that tremendous rhythm section

ctx.x: Spiritual. You must live spiritually. That's the motivating force.

You've always told me about Walter Page. You know I knew him very well and he was like my master and I worshiped him. I know how you felt about him, but tell me a little more about him. I just want to hear from you because I could never get enough of listening to what you have to say about Walter Page and working with Bill Basie and Freddie Green in that tremendous rhythm section.

You see, Milt, when we went to work nobody spoke to us. We never played with the band; we played with ourselves. I don't care, with the four of us, if three people were down, one person was up. If two people, if three people, but one person on four cylinders, one person was up - we never heard the band. We concentrated on ourselves and you know what that concentration was - living with peoples that we had to satisfy. We were the frosting, fix not on the cake - we were the sugar. You taste a cake and you ain't got…

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Whenever you saw a Duke Ellington... - that's Bennie Moten. You see Basie, that's Bennie Moten.

ctx.x: And the second one was your daughter. What's her name?

Joanne. When my first was born, Milt, I was making $5 a week with comebacks. You know what a comeback is? All right, now I'm going to tell you something. I have it in my scrapbook. We were working at the Peacock Inn at 19th and Farnum; stayed there 30 weeks with Jimmy Jones's band. Now we were making we started out at thought around $35 a week. We begin to get letters from Ben Webster, from Paul Webster, from Basie, from everybody.
* a tip, money in the kitty

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Who brought Basie - Walter Page? [INTERVIEWEE] Yes.

ctx.x: the first one to leave the band, right? Jimmie, to go to Bennie Moten, and then he brought Basie in.
